name: Oral hygiene for scent
summary: Mouth care aimed at fresh breath as part of overall scent; interventions have tentative but weak evidence.
lead: Oral hygiene for scent refers to caring for the mouth so that breath does not detract from how a person smells to others. Roughly 85 to 90 percent of genuine bad-breath cases originate in the mouth, most commonly from bacteria on the back of the tongue.

name: Pheromone sprays (Human Pheromone Sciences)
summary: Commercial sprays marketed as human sex pheromones; peer-reviewed research has not shown human pheromones change behavior.
lead: Pheromone sprays are commercial fragrance products marketed as containing human sex pheromones that increase attractiveness. Human Pheromone Sciences is named as a seller of such products.

name: Androstadienone / copulins claims
summary: The idea that sweat steroids and vaginal acids work as human attraction chemicals; lab effects on mood are reported, behavior change is unshown.
lead: Androstadienone is a steroid found in human sweat, semen and other body secretions, and copulins are a group of volatile fatty acids found in vaginal fluid. Both have been proposed as human pheromones, meaning chemical signals that could change the behavior or physiology of other people without conscious awareness.

name: Natural musk and scent on skin theory
summary: The belief that your own skin scent is an attraction signal worth protecting; odor research exists, the looksmaxxing claim itself is untested.
lead: The natural musk and scent-on-skin theory is the belief in appearance communities that a person's own body odor, and how a chosen scent interacts with their skin, is a meaningful part of attractiveness. Proponents frame natural scent as a signal that perfumes or deodorants can mask or enhance.

name: Unscented products for natural scent
summary: Fragrance-free grooming so your own smell isn't clashing with cologne; attraction benefit is untested, allergy reasons are documented.
lead: Using unscented or fragrance-free products is a grooming practice in which people choose soaps, deodorants and lotions without added fragrance, so that their own skin scent is not mixed with or overwhelmed by a perfume or cologne. In appearance communities it is discussed as a way to avoid fragrance clash.

name: Hair dye / bleaching
summary: Bleaching or dyeing hair to change contrast; well-established cosmetic method with allergy and damage risks.
lead: Hair coloring changes the color of head hair, typically to cover gray, change a look or restore color after bleaching or sun exposure. In looksmaxxing and style discussions it is raised as a way to alter contrast, for example bleaching hair lighter or dyeing it darker. Reports say 50 to 80 percent of women in the US, Europe and Japan have used hair dye.

name: Wardrobe capsule / minimalist wardrobe
summary: A small set of interchangeable, well-fitting basics; a long-standing fashion idea with no attractiveness studies behind it.
lead: A capsule wardrobe is a small collection of clothes that can be combined into many outfits, usually built from staple items in coordinating colors. In looksmaxxing and style communities it is discussed as a way to dress well with a few well-fitting, interchangeable basics.

name: Old money / quiet luxury style
summary: Logo-free, tailored, high-quality dressing that signals wealth discreetly; popular aesthetic, no attractiveness studies.
lead: Quiet luxury is a style of dress marked by understated elegance, high-quality materials, timeless design and no visible logos. It is often used interchangeably with old money style or stealth wealth, though commentators use the terms differently. Old money itself refers to a social class of families that have kept wealth across generations.

name: Streetwear / techwear style
summary: Hip-hop, skate and outdoor-gear-derived casual dressing; a style choice with no studies on attractiveness effects.
lead: Streetwear is a casual clothing style that spread worldwide in the 1990s, drawing on sportswear, skateboarding, surf culture, punk, hip-hop and Japanese street fashion. Many labels build demand through limited releases and restricted supply, which has fed a resale market.

name: Preppy / Ivy style
summary: Oxford shirts, chinos and loafers from Ivy League campus dress; a style choice with no attractiveness studies behind it.
lead: Preppy is a style of dress associated with graduates of Northeastern US college-preparatory schools and with upper-class and old-money backgrounds. Its menswear root, Ivy style, began in the early 1900s and was widespread by the late 1950s, named for Ivy League campuses.

name: Fit-focused dressing for body type (shoulder-to-waist illusion)
summary: Cuts and fit chosen to show off a V-taper; popular in style advice, untested as a clothing intervention.
lead: Fit-focused dressing refers to choosing garment cuts that emphasise a V-shaped torso, with wide shoulders and a narrower waist, and that minimise features a wearer sees as flaws. The inverted-triangle (V) shape is one of the male body shape categories, described as wider shoulders and chest with a narrow waist.

name: Vertical stripes / monochrome elongation
summary: Dressing in vertical stripes or one colour to look taller and slimmer; the small perception literature points the other way for stripes.
lead: Vertical stripes and single-colour outfits are a common piece of style advice, based on the belief that they make a person look taller and slimmer, while horizontal stripes make them look shorter and wider. Researchers have examined the underlying visual illusion, and the results are mixed.

name: Photo angle maxxing
summary: Choosing angle, distance, lens and tilt to photograph well; the lens-distance physics is documented, attractiveness effects are untested.
lead: Photo angle maxxing is the practice of finding the camera angle, subject distance, lens and head tilt that make a person look best in photographs. It sits in looksmaxxing communities alongside photography and lighting discussion.
claims: Standing back with a real camera looks better than a close selfie.

name: Camera lens distortion (portrait lens 85mm)
summary: Using a longer lens from farther back to reduce nose and face distortion; the optics are well documented.
lead: Perspective distortion in photographs makes features nearest the lens look larger. A face photographed close up with a wide-angle lens makes the nose appear bigger relative to the rest of the face, while a telephoto lens used from farther away makes it appear smaller.

name: Photo lighting / golden hour
summary: Shooting in soft, low-angle light to flatter your face on camera; physics is clear, the attractiveness payoff is untested.
lead: Golden hour is the period shortly after sunrise or before sunset when daylight is redder and softer than at midday. Photographers use it because low sun passes through more atmosphere, lowering contrast and weakening direct light.
claims: Soft golden-hour light makes faces look more attractive in photos

name: Dating-profile photo optimization
summary: Picking and ordering dating photos with data from strangers' votes; popular idea, little independent testing.
lead: Dating-profile photo optimization is the practice of selecting, editing and ordering photographs for dating apps using feedback or data, rather than personal preference alone. In looksmaxxing communities it is most often associated with Photofeeler, a site where anonymous voters rate photos on attractiveness, trustworthiness and smartness.
claims: Rated-best photos do not necessarily perform best on dating apps
Raters over-reward smiling

name: Photofeeler testing
summary: Crowd-rating of your photos by strangers; popular as a looks scoreboard, with disputed real-world meaning.
lead: Photofeeler testing is the practice of uploading a photograph to Photofeeler, a website where anonymous voters rate it, in order to see how strangers perceive the person pictured. Photofeeler was founded in 2013 in Boulder, Colorado, by Ben Peterson and Ann Pierce, and offers business, social and dating test types.
claims: Photofeeler scores are a fair measure of how attractive you are
High Photofeeler scores do not translate into dating-app success
Voters are biased toward smiling photos

name: Glasses frame selection by face shape
summary: Choosing frames to balance your face; widely repeated styling idea with no testing behind it.
lead: Glasses frame selection by face shape is a style practice in which people pick frame shapes intended to balance or complement their face, for example choosing frames to add a perceived 'hunter eyes' look. Wikipedia notes that people often choose frames based on how they look on the wearer.

name: Glasses to mask facial flaws
summary: Using chunky frames to hide bags, asymmetry or a nose; a styling trick with no research behind it.
lead: Glasses to mask facial flaws is a style practice of wearing thick or large frames to draw attention from features a person dislikes, such as eye bags, asymmetry or the nose. Wikipedia describes glasses as now widely worn as fashion accessories, including non-prescription pairs.

name: Colored lenses / blue light glasses
summary: Tinted blue-light lenses sold for eye strain and fresher-looking eyes; eye-care bodies cited by Wikipedia do not recommend them.
lead: Colored lenses and blue-light glasses are spectacles with tinted or filtered lenses marketed to reduce eye strain from screens and, in some looksmaxxing circles, to reduce puffiness around the eyes. By the late 2010s such glasses became popular, with claims ranging from dry eyes and eye strain to sleep disruption and macular degeneration.
claims: Blue-light glasses reduce eye strain and eye puffiness

name: Skin-tone matching foundation / BB cream for men
summary: Light base makeup used to even out skin tone; mainstream in cosmetics, with little research on male appearance outcomes.
lead: Skin-tone matching foundation and BB cream are tinted base products applied to the face to even out complexion and cover blemishes. Foundation is a long-established cosmetic category, while BB cream ("blemish balm" or "beauty balm") is a lighter hybrid intended to combine coverage, moisturizer and sun protection in one step.
claims: Light BB cream or foundation evens skin tone and hides redness or marks in a natural-looking way.
A properly shade-matched product is hard to detect.

name: Men's makeup (contour, bronzer, highlight)
summary: Subtle shading and highlighting aimed at sharpening the jaw and cheekbones; documented in makeup practice but unstudied for male attractiveness.
lead: Men's makeup in this context refers to using contour (darker shades), highlighter (lighter shades) and bronzer to emphasize the jaw, cheekbones and nose. Contouring generally uses a shade one or two tones darker than the skin in hollows and along edges to create shadow, while highlighting uses lighter shades on prominent areas.
claims: Contour and highlight can make the jaw and cheekbones look more defined.
Makeup carries stigma for men that limits its use.

name: Lip balm / tinted lip color
summary: Wax-based lip moisturizers, sometimes tinted, used for healthier-looking lips; common and low-risk, with limited appearance research.
lead: Lip balm is a wax-like product that moisturizes and protects dry or chapped lips by forming a barrier layer. Tinted versions add color for a natural lip shade. Common bases include beeswax, candelilla and carnauba wax, lanolin, paraffin and petrolatum, sometimes with sunscreen, flavoring or dyes.
claims: Regular lip balm keeps lips looking healthier and fuller.
Lip balm is addictive.

name: Teeth whitening before photos
summary: Fast-acting whitening (strips, trays, in-office) timed before photographs; effective short term but with sensitivity and rebound.
lead: Teeth whitening before photos refers to using bleaching products or professional treatment shortly before a photo shoot or event to brighten teeth. Methods include dentist-applied peroxide gels, tray-based gels, strips, whitening toothpastes and rinses.
claims: Whitening shortly before photos gives an immediately brighter smile.
Light-activated whitening works better.

name: Undercut / fade with textured top
summary: A short-sided haircut with longer styled top, widely recommended for many face shapes; popularity is documented, attractiveness effects unstudied.
lead: The undercut is a hairstyle in which the sides and back are shaved or clipped very short while the top is left long, often parted and styled. A fade tapers the sides gradually, and a textured top refers to the longer hair styled with product for volume or a matte finish.
claims: This cut flatters many face shapes.
Skin fades make the face and jaw look sharper.

name: Buzz cut for thinning hair
summary: Clipping hair very short to make thinning or receding hair less noticeable; widely used, with mixed research on how bald and shaved looks are perceived.
lead: A buzz cut is a very short hairstyle, usually clipped to a uniform length across the head. Wikipedia notes it is popular among people with thinning or receding hairlines. "Shaving down" refers to adopting it to reduce the contrast between thinning and denser areas.
claims: A buzz cut hides thinning more effectively than longer hair.
A shaved head can read as confident or dominant.

name: Hair length for face shape (long hair maxxing)
summary: Matching hair length and shape to your face outline; popular style advice with no dedicated trials behind it.
lead: Choosing hair length to suit the shape of the face, and growing hair longer to frame or soften facial features, is a style practice discussed in appearance-focused communities under labels such as "long hair maxxing". The idea is that length, volume and parting change how the outline of the face, jaw and forehead are perceived.

name: Facial hair as camouflage (weak chin)
summary: Using a beard to mask a recessed chin; widely practiced, but no study has tested the camouflage claim itself.
lead: Facial hair as camouflage refers to growing a beard to mask a recessed chin or weak jawline. Proponents say beard shape and density add apparent projection and definition to the lower face.

name: Posture awareness
summary: Consciously standing and sitting tall to look more present; posture research is about pain, not attractiveness.
lead: Posture awareness is the practice of noticing and correcting how one stands and sits, for example keeping the head over the shoulders and the spine upright. In appearance-focused communities it is discussed as a way to look taller, more confident and more "present", and to counter the head-forward posture associated with phone and desk use.

name: Body language / presence training
summary: Training stance, eye contact and pace to look more confident; the research supports felt confidence more than outcomes.
lead: Body language or presence training is the deliberate practice of nonverbal behaviour, such as an open stance, steady eye contact and slower movements, intended to make a person appear more confident or commanding. It is discussed in appearance communities alongside posture and grooming.
